slot.brief: Reversible gas-phase dissociation at known total equilibrium pressure; set up ICE table and compute degree of dissociation then Kp.

stem: Pure $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)$ at $1.00$ bar reaches a total equilibrium pressure of $1.50$ bar at constant temperature and volume. Find $(\alpha,K_p)$ for $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)\rightleftharpoons2\text{NO}_2(g)$.

verdicts.working: At constant temperature and volume, total pressure is proportional to total moles: 1.50 = 1.00(1 + α), so α = 0.50. The equilibrium partial pressures are p(NO₂) = 1.00 bar and p(N₂O₄) = 0.50 bar. Thus Kₚ = p(NO₂)²/p(N₂O₄) = 2.00 bar.

working:
Let initial amount be $n_0$; ICE change is $-\alpha n_0,+2\alpha n_0$.
$P_{	ext{eq}}=P_0(1+\alpha)\Rightarrow\alpha=1.50/1.00-1=0.50$.
$p_{	ext{N}_2	ext{O}_4}=P_0(1-\alpha)=0.50$ bar; $p_{	ext{NO}_2}=2P_0\alpha=1.00$ bar.
$K_p=\dfrac{p_{	ext{NO}_2}^2}{p_{	ext{N}_2	ext{O}_4}}=2.00$ bar.

Independent check: At constant temperature and volume, total pressure is proportional to total moles: 1.50 = 1.00(1 + α), so α = 0.50. The equilibrium partial pressures are p(NO₂) = 1.00 bar and p(N₂O₄) = 0.50 bar. Thus Kₚ = p(NO₂)²/p(N₂O₄) = 2.00 bar.
solution:
At constant $T,V$, pressure is proportional to total moles; hence $P_{\rm eq}=P_0(1+\alpha)$, giving $\alpha=1.50/1.00-1=0.50$$.\nThe$ equilibrium partial pressures are $p_{\mathrm{NO_2}}=2P_0\alpha=1.00$ bar and $p_{\mathrm{N_2O_4}}=P_0(1-\alpha)=0.50$ bar.
$$K_p=\frac{p_{\mathrm{NO_2}}^2}{p_{\mathrm{N_2O_4}}}=\frac{(1.00)^2}{0.50}=2.00\ \text{bar}$$
